project.summary: The task tree has two dimensions: (1) Process — how we work: source discovery → feature extraction → spec generation → replay implementation → execution → model feedback. Each process step carries knowledge about the methodology. (2) Domain — what we know: per-feature understanding of AKS behavior, organized by feature family. Domain knowledge currently lives in model/knowledge-map/model.json and features/*.yaml. Future: domain branches in the tree for deeper per-feature exploration. When a task is accepted, it gains knowledge. When archived, execution detail is lost but knowledge rolls up to the parent. Any branch can be reopened for deeper exploration.

context.throughput_rule: Keep smart execution-frontier selection active: one task chooses high-ROI existing specs/suites and creates/activates runner leaves; runner leaves execute through native spec-runner/suite machinery with precise conflict scopes.

user_steering_20260609_smart_execution.summary: User steering: push the project toward real test execution and feedback, but do not bypass the project system. The project already supports plan/spec/suite execution; use those capabilities instead of building another runner or manually executing tests from outside the task engine.
principles: Use existing bun run plan/spec/suite/generate capabilities as the execution substrate.
Tests are slow, so select high-ROI specs and amortize compatible specs into shared cluster lifecycles.
Run independent specs/suites in parallel only when conflict scopes, resource groups, feature flags, and cleanup scopes do not overlap.
Every real run must produce runs/executions artifacts, evidence/archive artifacts, diagnosis, cleanup state, and model/spec feedback.
Do not confuse dry-run/local check/runner resolution with real e2e verification.

planner-context-quality.goal: Improve the planning packet so the planner LLM has enough information to make correct decisions without retry loops. The planner created 11 duplicate tasks for a path already at staging-pass because the packet didn't include path status.

context.root_cause: The planning packet (from planningPacket() in SDK) shows frontier task IDs and state counts, but does NOT include model path status. The LLM sees a path name in context but doesn't know it's already staging-pass. The deterministic seeder correctly excludes staging-pass — the LLM needs the same view.
context.evidence: net-integration-authorized-service-tags retried 11 times (frontier-20260616-1 through -11). Path was staging-pass since 04:49. Planner kept creating tasks because it didn't know.
context.principle: The infrastructure provides information. The LLM decides. Don't add guards to block wrong decisions — give the LLM the knowledge to decide correctly.
context.fix_direction: Include compact model status in the planning packet: passing count, non-passing paths with their status and root cause. The LLM then knows what's done and what actually needs work.
